title: Disaggregated Fairness Metrics Pattern
description: A pattern for measuring and disclosing a risk-scoring model's error rates separately by protected group, and documenting the justification for any proxy variable used, rather than relying on a single aggregate accuracy figure.
problem: A risk-scoring model can look accurate on an aggregate metric while its false-positive and false-negative rates differ substantially across protected groups, or while it relies on a proxy variable (e.g. cost as a stand-in for need) that itself encodes historical inequity.
solution: Report false-positive rate, false-negative rate, and calibration separately for each protected group the model may legally be tested against; document every proxy variable used in place of the true outcome of interest, with an explicit assessment of whether it correlates with a protected characteristic; and re-run this analysis whenever the model or its training data changes materially.
applicability: Any model that produces a risk, priority, or eligibility score used to inform a high-stakes decision about an individual — criminal justice, healthcare, credit, hiring, or benefits eligibility.
consequences: Requires access to demographic data for testing purposes, which itself must be governed carefully; disaggregation can surface tensions between competing fairness definitions (e.g. equal calibration vs. equal error rates) that have no single objectively 'correct' resolution and require a documented, deliberate choice.

citations.title: Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations

relationships.reason: Disaggregated metrics are the concrete mechanism satisfying this control's impact-identification requirement.
The pattern's output is a fairness metrics report.
